name: PLANT GROWTH CHAMBER
desc: ISO and CE Certified Double-Walled Plant Growth Chamber engineered for high-precision simulation of ecological environments. Features a 340-liter SS304 internal volume, dynamic humidity control, and high-intensity 3-side illumination up to 23000 LUX driven by a weekly digital cycle timer.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Plant Growth Chamber is a precision-controlled environmental simulation system that integrates a CFC-free EMERSON Copeland refrigeration circuit, tubular air heaters, an SS304 boiler humidification module, and 3-side LED lighting to reproduce dynamic diurnal and seasonal regimes. The chamber operates on dual PID loops that compare process value (PV) feedback from solid-state sensors against user-defined set values (SV), modulating compressor, heater, and steam injection to maintain temperature within ±1% and relative humidity within ±3% RH. Forced air circulation through balanced axial fan arrays ensures uniform distribution, while a 24×7 programmable digital cycle timer regulates photoperiod up to 23,000 LUX to drive photosynthesis, photomorphogenesis, and photoperiodic flowering. Botanists, agronomists, plant pathologists, and PhD/MSc/BSc researchers use this platform for Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, Zea mays, Solanum lycopersicum and Nicotiana benthamiana cultivation, in vitro tissue culture on Murashige and Skoog (MS) agar supplemented with sucrose, auxins (IAA, NAA) and cytokinins (BAP, kinetin), seed germination testing under ISTA and OECD 208 protocols, plant-microbe interaction assays with Pseudomonas syringae, Fusarium oxysporum, Botrytis cinerea and Rhizobium inoculants, and VOC/headspace studies where plants emit ethylene, terpenoids and green leaf volatiles under controlled humidity from 50 to 90% RH. Compliance with ISO 9001, CE, and relevant ASTM E1706/E1714 environmental simulation standards supports reproducible phytotron research.
sop: Verify the chamber is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz single-phase earthed mains supply and that the outer door lock, inner glass door, and caster wheel brakes are engaged before powering ON the main isolator.

Inspect the internal SS304 chamber for any previous debris, wipe shelves with 70% ethanol, and ensure the external water reservoir is filled with deionized or distilled water for the automated humidity replenishment loop.

On the temperature PID controller, press the 'SET' button once until the SV indicator flashes. Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target temperature (e.g., 22°C for Arabidopsis; 28°C for rice). Press 'SET' again to lock the value.

On the humidity PID controller, press the 'SET' button once. Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target relative humidity (e.g., 60–70% RH for most crops). Press 'SET' again to lock the value.

Configure the 24×7 weekly programmable digital cycle timer for the desired photoperiod (e.g., 16 hours light / 8 hours dark) and select the required illumination intensity using the LED lighting block switches.

Load plant material, tissue culture vessels, or seed germination trays onto the height-adjustable stainless steel shelves, maintaining at least 5 cm spacing between containers for unrestricted forced-air circulation; close the inner glass door and then the insulated outer door securely.
Switch ON the lighting and confirm that the temperature and humidity controllers display stable PV values close to the locked SV targets; record initial readings in the logbook.

Allow a stabilization period of 30–90 minutes, then verify that no temperature or humidity deviation alarms are active and that the compressor, heater, and steam generator are cycling normally via the PID indicators.
At the end of the daily session, check the water reservoir level, inspect door gaskets for condensation or leaks, and wipe any external moisture with a dry lint-free cloth.

SAFETY WARNING: Never place flammable solvents, strong acids, or volatile corrosive chemicals inside the chamber; always power OFF and unplug the unit before cleaning or maintenance, and if a temperature/humidity alarm sounds, do not open the doors abruptly—quarantine samples and notify the laboratory supervisor to prevent thermal shock and contamination.
